fixes.was: GDS holds no central record of the AI models departments use. It relies on the Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard, and further Cabinet Office activity is planned. The Prime Minister's AI Taskforce will not publish annual reports. Questions on Chinese AI models drew only general answers: discussions with US counterparts are not disclosed, and the AI Biosecurity Lab will assess security before approving any technology. Spencer has since tabled a question on whether the Cabinet Office uses Chinese open-weight models (UIN 45816).
fixes.now: There is no central tracking of AI model use within government. The Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard publishes information on in-scope algorithmic tools, and further Cabinet Office activity is planned. The Prime Minister's AI Taskforce does not intend to publish formal annual reports. Questions on Chinese AI models drew general answers: details of confidential discussions with US counterparts are not routinely disclosed, and the Government will work with the independent AI Biosecurity Lab on robust security arrangements, including assessment of technology before approval for use. Spencer tabled a question on 23 November asking whether the Cabinet Office uses open-weight AI models published by developers based in China (UIN 45816).
fixes.reason: The draft turns an intention into a categorical promise, overstates nondisclosure and assigns an approval responsibility not stated in HL5232. ATRS is not an exhaustive model register.
